A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 20, from an error in converting $\text{nm}$ and $\text{mm}$ to $\text{m}$ when using $x = \lambda D / a$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from a power-of-ten error in $\lambda = 550 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ or $a = 0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: Half the correct spacing, from using $2a$ instead of $a$ or halving $\lambda D / a$.

D.explanation: Correct fringe spacing from $x = \lambda D / a$ with $\lambda = 550 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $D = 4.0 \text{ m}$ and $a = 0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

hints: Notice the double-slit values actually given: slit separation $a = 0.50 \text{ mm}$, wall distance $D = 4.0 \text{ m}$ and wavelength $\lambda = 550 \text{ nm}$.
Connect fringe spacing to the two-source interference relation $x = \lambda D / a$, where larger $D$ or $\lambda$ widens fringes and larger $a$ narrows them.
Convert $\lambda$ and $a$ to metres before dividing, then check the result is in metres and convert to $\text{mm}$ to compare with the four options.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $a = 0.50 \text{ mm} = 0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $D = 4.0 \text{ m}$, $\lambda = 550 \text{ nm} = 550 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
State the governing rule for adjacent bright fringes in two-source interference: $x = \lambda D / a$.
Substitute with units: $x = (550 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m})(4.0 \text{ m}) / (0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m})$.
Calculate the numerator: $(550 \times 10^{-9}) \times 4.0 = 2.2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$, then divide by $0.50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to get $x = 4.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Convert to millimetres: $4.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 4.4 \text{ mm}$, which matches the calculated fringe separation. This is option D.
